claims.scope: Full RM0522 chapter13 pages371–381 read. Literal family matrices filtered against exact C542 declarations; no executable interconnect profile or whole-device closure.

contracts.detail: Table84 footnote2 explicitly makes connections unavailable when a peripheral is absent. Exact header/DS establish TIM1/2/6/7/8/12/15, ADC1, COMP1/2, DAC1, LPDMA1/2 and other listed exact instances. TIM3/4/5/16/17, ADC2/3 and DAC2 are not instantiated. Header DMA channels0..3 exclude Table85 LPDMA1 channel4..7 rows. Excluded literal rows remain retained for provenance.

ADC12 is family/common-domain notation, not proof of a physical ADC2. Exact ADC1 and ADC12_COMMON are separate register views/dependencies of the conversion subsystem. LPDMA12 is a destination group for two existing controllers, not a third controller. DAC rows map only to DAC1 ownership; the Table85 channel1 rows do not independently authorize channel2. Source identity is separate from supported mode.

Retain one owner for each source peripheral, destination peripheral and shared configuration field. Fanout does not duplicate the source timer, comparator, oscillator, clock divider or physical EXTI line. A destination input mux selects a source; it does not grant independent simultaneous ownership to all listed sources. GPIO-origin EXTI routes share the same physical line across ports and CPU/DMA/ADC/DAC consumers. Preserve the hash-bound accepted composition as-is.

A/S/I/B are literal family matrix classifications. S requires synchronous clocks; arbitrary RCC selections do not establish that precondition. A admits sampling jitter. B no-latency prose does not waive timer break filters, clock-dependent synchronizers, enable/polarity propagation, MOE/AOE or delayed protection modes. No numerical zero-latency end-to-end contract is admitted. Run/Sleep/Stop support is explicitly peripheral-dependent.

Preserve each timer ITR, TI, ETR, OCREF clear and break input as a distinct destination. TRGO and TRGO2 are different producer controls. BKIN fanout is not another timer's software break command, and system-fault compound rows do not define individual selectors. Absent-producer rows are excluded before considering generic SDK encodings. Presence-only rows still inherit destination mode, clock, filter, output and lock conditions.

ADC regular and injected trigger inputs remain distinct; internal VREFINT and VSENSE identities are analog paths, not external GPIO routes. Table85 VIN13/12 names agree with ADC1 connectivity but do not resolve DAC loopback ambiguity. DAC hold clock lists LSI or LSE; this is selection notation, not proof both clocks may be combined. Table158 additionally lists EXTI9 trigger12 and channelx=1,2, absent from the chapter13 detail inventory; channel2 capability conflict remains a separate gate.

Table85 LPDMA trigger edges are distinct from hardware transfer requests and channel capabilities. EXTI0..7 need exact port/pin/line/polarity ownership and the existing unresolved trigger-stage gate. A completion trigger cannot prove the producer request, memory visibility or completed peripheral transaction. Cyclic chains and fanout require independently bounded lifetime and arbitration. No expanded hardware-request or trigger profile is admitted.

Table369 resolves generic Table85 LPDMA channel1 trigger to LPDMA1 channel1 TC. LPTIM external trigger, counter input and capture muxes are distinct. CPU EVENTOUT is retained as an internal source label; it does not by itself grant a package EVENTOUT AF route or prove event delivery. CRS source0 is GPIO SYNC,1 LSE,2 USB SOF,3 HSE-derived1MHz; USB SOF availability, HSE divider and frequency-evaluation prerequisites remain separate.

Table85 lists only COMP1 blanking. Exact COMP2 exists, but its routes must use its own mapping, including different TIM1 output selection and LPTIM blanking in LL. No blanket replication of COMP1 rows to COMP2. ES2.4.1 prohibits simultaneous operation on RevZ and not RevY; physical revision remains unknown. Internal analog mux, clock, enable, stabilization and EXTI gates remain applicable.

source_derived_SDK_gates.detail: Generic LL constants and exact header presence support bounded source candidates, not cross-peripheral execution. In particular TIM8 ADC1 fallback, COMP2 trigger36 and timer COMP2 selections require conflict-specific resolution. No arbitrary C guard evaluation or symbol-name-to-selector inference is used for Table85 presence filtering.

conflicts.detail: Table85 RM375 connects fdcan1_rxeof_evt to TIM2 tim_ti2_in7; timer Table311 RM1138 instead names fdcan1_txeof_evt. Preserve RX versus TX disagreement; do not normalize silently. LL TIM2 TI2 FDCAN1 TXEOF agrees with the local timer chapter, while TI1 uses RXEOF. This is not a second FDCAN2 source on TI1/TI2; separate TIM2 TI3/TI4 inputs carry FDCAN2 events.

Table85 RM376 and timer RM960 connect TIM8 ETR3..5 to ADC2 AWD1..3, absent on exact C542. Pinned LL conditionally falls back to ADC1 for those selectors. Presence of ADC1 does not establish that fallback in silicon. These Table85 rows remain excluded with an explicit SDK conflict.

Table84 marks I3C-to-TIM12, TIM2-to-LPDMA1/2 and COMP-to-LPTIM1/LPDMA1/2 as no interconnect, while Table85 supplies I3C1 IBI acknowledge, TIM2 TRGO and COMP1 paths. A summary dash is not silently replaced by a runtime edge; retain both source levels. Additional exact-endpoint discrepancies: LPDMA1-to-LPTIM1 is a summary dash, but Table85 generic LPDMA trigger5 is identified as LPDMA1 channel1 TC by Table369; LSI-to-DAC is a dash while Table85 DAC hold clock names ck_lsi OR ck_lse. TIM2_CH2-to-TIM2 TI2 input0 versus the summary diagonal dash is an external-channel/default-input scope difference, not evidence of internal self-trigger routing.

Table84 TIM8-to-COMP is I while TIM1/TIM2/TIM15-to-COMP are A; Table85 describes timer OC blanking signals for all. Generic analog-endpoint definition alone does not establish why those routes differ or a latency bound.

Chapter13 is not an exhaustive exact route inventory. Local tables additionally list COMP2 to TIM1/TIM8 TI1 input2, break comparator2, break2 comparator2 and OCREF clear1; TIM2 TI1 input2 and TI4 input2; TIM12 TI1 input2; TIM15 TI1 input2; LPTIM1 input2 mux1. TIM2 TI3 input7 FDCAN2 RXEOF and TI4 input7 FDCAN2 TXEOF are distinct from TIM2 TI1/TI2 FDCAN1. Local TIM15 FDCAN2 input6 conflicts with LL selector7. DAC EXTI9 and LPTIM GPIO/default routes are also omitted. Separate SDK-only candidates COMP2 DMA selector36 and TIM15 COMP2 break are not promoted to RM-supported routing. TIM1/TIM8 COMP2 ETR2 conflicts with RM reserved encoding. All additions require destination-specific contracts and COMP revision gating.

Table85 calls selector18 comp1_out; Table94 calls it comp1_out_dma. Their identical selector is evidence of a naming correspondence, not proof which pre/post-filter stage is delivered. Chapter13 ends DMA triggers at31, Table94 adds32..35 for absent channels4..7; LL additionally exposes COMP2 selector36, absent from both RM tables. No automatic source-stage or selector36 admission.

RM380 prints tim8_tgo2 and tim12_tgo for injected selectors17/18, while timer sources and ADC trigger table use TRGO naming. Original spellings remain in raw rows; no new producer is instantiated from a typo. RM378 generic lpdma_ch1_tcf is separately qualified by Table369 as lpdma1_ch1_tc.

RM960 Table288 reserves ETR selector2 for TIM1/TIM8. LL defines COMP2 for both using TIM_AF1_ETRSEL_1; exact header evaluates that macro to0x02 shifted14, raw selector2. Macro spelling alone is not used to infer encoding. COMP2 presence does not resolve this route conflict.

Table85 compound source cell has raw line-separated PWM_SAFE, LOCKUP, PVD, RAM, ECC; token boundaries/wiring are not inferred from those line breaks. Table292 instead identifies LOCKUP (CLL), SRAM double ECC (SEL), PVD (PVDL), non-volatile memory double ECC (ECCL), and CSS always enabled with no SBS enable bit. PWM_SAFE is not a named Table292 row; CSS absent from Table85 compound cell and ECC classes not explicitly distinguished. Preserve source scopes and require SBS/timer contract; do not create five independent selector routes from flattened text.

On absent exact-device endpoints only: MCO1/MCO2-to-TIM16 and I3C-to-TIM17 have summary dashes but detail rows. TIM2/TIM5/TIM12-to-TIM16/17 summary S cells have no matching Table85 detail rows. These remain excluded family context, not exact-device features.

connection_classes.A: Source sampled by destination clock; possible latency jitter
connection_classes.S: Source/destination synchronous; RM describes deterministic latency without jitter
connection_classes.I: Either endpoint is an analog signal
connection_classes.B: Combinational break/fault path; RM describes no latency
connection_classes.-: No interconnect according to summary table

finite_source_maps.class_qualification: Literal RM371 classifications, not numerical end-to-end latency guarantees. Clock-domain equality, filters and mode must be established separately.

extraction.method: extract_tables default line-grid extraction; exact header width/order assertions; rotated destination headings reversed and checked against explicit column order; destination-only merged cells forward-filled within each page; original cells retained
extraction.visual_confirmation: Partial: RM372 retained image inspected for column order and named summary conflicts; all244 detail rows and RM373 remain text/grid checked only.

finite_source_maps.qualification: Literal finite source rows and presence filtering only. No selector writes, clock admission, GPIO assignment or runtime integration.

non_peripheral_source_presence.CPU: Exact Cortex-M33 core, not a peripheral instance.

source_aliases.qualification: Identity correspondence only; USB_SOF delivery requires active USB configuration.
GPIO bank presence is not package bonding. extiN rows require existing single physical EXTI line owner; direct BKIN/CRS input rows require bonded AF pins. No blanket GPIO-to-EXTI equivalence.
Clock/MCO signal selection and enabled source are separate from register instance presence.
EVENTOUT source is not an instantiated peripheral or a proof of event delivery.

naming_correspondences.qualification: Source spelling correspondence candidate only; clock divider/rate not established from the name.
Table85 versus local TIM12 table naming; no added route or trigger delivery claim.
Named source correspondence only; no clock or pin operational claim.
CPU event label correspondence, separate from package EVENTOUT AF and delivered timing.
Generic Table85 producer qualified by local Table369 to LPDMA1 channel1; not LPDMA2 or hardware request.

summary_scope_exclusions.qualification: GPIO and CPU have no Table84 source row. These are summary omissions, not dash contradictions. Some destinations are absent and stay excluded.

open_gates: Full chapter read and literal table inventory do not establish every relationship on exact silicon. Partial RM372 visual check and independent text transcription review do not close all detail-cell visual review.
All source clocks, asynchronous stages, edge delivery, arbitration, latching, filter/reset and pending-event behavior require destination-specific contracts.
No package bonding, GPIO AF/electrical or board path is admitted merely from an internal source label. Hash-bound package records remain unchanged.
Existing accepted EXTI physical line resources and composition profiles remain unchanged. No production catalog or runtime changes.
No full mode-combination, cyclic-chain, performance, build or hardware qualification.

Compound system-break raw cell and local Table292 remain separately retained; line breaks do not establish separate signal boundaries or selector wiring. Exact SBS/timer protection controls remain required.

visual_checks.scope: Retained root-rendered image inspected by author and independent root reviewer: destination order and named summary dash/class conflicts. Not an exhaustive visual audit of all244 detail rows or p373.
